Question_text: SWB is in the secondary sector. It produces 150000 wooden bookcases each week using batch production. SWB sells all its output to one customer. Quality control is important. SWB has 240 employees, of which 100 are part-time workers. SWB's managers use noticeboards around the factory and meetings with employees every month to help reduce communication barriers. The Operations Manager is considering introducing just-in-time inventory control to reduce the amount of waste.
Sub_topic: Features, benefits, limitations: job, batch, flow production
How barriers arise, problems of ineffective communication

Parts.part_text: Define 'secondary sector'.
Identify two factors a business should consider when deciding whether to introduce just-in-time inventory control.
Outline one advantage and one disadvantage to SWB of using quality control.
Explain two possible communication barriers that might exist at SWB.
Do you think it is a good idea for a business to have only one customer? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Tom started ALB 5 years ago making trainers (sneakers) out of sustainable materials such as wool. One of ALB's objectives is to protect the environment. As part of his research, Tom calculated some costs which he could use in his break-even analysis. An extract is shown in Figure 2.1. ALB uses retailers to distribute its products. Tom thinks a successful entrepreneur has to be a good manager.
image: Bar chart titled 'Fig. 2.1' showing cost percentages for ALB. Categories are: retailers' costs (50%), manufacturers' profit (5%), fixed costs (15%), variable costs (30%). The X-axis is 'percent' from 0 to 60. The Y-axis lists the cost categories.
Topic: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis
Sub_topic: Classify costs: fixed, variable, average, total
Advantages, disadvantages of channels: wholesalers, retailers, direct
Functions: planning, organising, coordinating, commanding, controlling

Parts.part_text: Define 'variable costs'.
Identify two limitations of break-even analysis.
Outline two possible advantages to ALB of using retailers to distribute its products.
Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to ALB of trying to protect the environment.
Do you think a successful entrepreneur has to be a good manager? Justify your answer.

Question_text: Aurelie is a sole trader. She started her small hotel 1 year ago using government support. Aurelie knew it would be important to build good customer relationships. Aurelie wants to analyse her financial statements using ratio analysis. An extract is shown in Table 3.1. She is worried about how the Government's plan to introduce a new tourist tax of $1 per tourist per night might affect her business.
image: Table 3.1: Extract of Aurelie's Income statement for 2020 ($). It shows: Revenue 5600, Cost of sales 1800, Gross profit X, Expenses 2400, Profit Y.
Sub_topic: Features: revenue, cost of sales, gross profit, profit, retained profit
Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Government support for start-ups, grants, training schemes

Parts.part_text: Identify two ways a government can support new business start-ups.
Calculate X and Y.
State four financial ratios a business can use.
Explain two ways that the introduction of a new tourist tax might affect Aurelie's business.
Do you think offering good customer service is the best way for a small business to build customer relationships? Justify your answer.

Question_text: GCF is a public limited company. It provides a range of computer services to businesses including designing websites and creating apps. The Human Resources Director use ideas based on Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs to help keep GCF's 250 employees well-motivated. An extract of methods used is shown in Table 4.1. GCF plans to expand by taking over one of its competitors. This will cost $50m. To finance the takeover, GCF is considering issuing new shares.
image: Table 4.1: Extract of methods used at GCF to motivate employees. It lists two methods: 'Employee of the month' award and 'Organises team building courses'.
Sub_topic: Concept of human needs, Maslow’s hierarchy
Non-financial: job enrichment, rotation, teamworking, training, promotion
Features: sole traders, partnerships, private/public limited companies, franchises, joint ventures
Factors in choice: size, legal form, amount, time, loans
Methods of measuring size: employees, output, capital employed

Parts.part_text: Identify two features of a public limited company.
Identify the level of Maslow's Hierarchy of Needs each of the following methods belongs to. 'Employee of the month award':. Organises team building courses:
Outline two advantages to GCF of having well-motivated employees.
Explain one advantage and one disadvantage to GCF of issuing new shares as a source of finance.
Do you think the number of employees is the best way to measure the size of a tertiary sector business? Justify your answer.
